title: Ribbon runs: Boss receipt
summary: String runs. Return the position-weighted total.
revisit: Earlier foundation work; the first unit establishes the prerequisite
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`line` is text. A character is one letter, digit, space, or punctuation mark.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `runLengths`. A run is a group of matching characters next to each other. End a run only when the character changes or the text ends. Record the length of each run, from left to right. Spaces count as characters too. For "aa bb", `runLengths` is [2, 1, 2].
2. Multiply each number in `runLengths` by its position, counting from 1: the first number by 1, the second by 2, and so on.
3. Add those products. Store the sum in `weightedTotal`.
4. Complete `ribbonRunsBossReceipt` so it returns `weightedTotal`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `line` is "jp  pvb", then `runLengths` is [1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1] and `ribbonRunsBossReceipt` returns 24.

Rules
- If `runLengths` is empty, return 0.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `line` is "kuuow bnnnq".
TEST DATA 2: `line` is "UU uUU".

constraints: Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
The text uses ASCII characters (a basic character set). Only an ordinary space separates words.
Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the helper list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
